routeSelection.basis: Four equally weighted tracks are available for the generic degree. Systematic Theology is first in the adopted regulations. The example uses the biblical-language route in the main curriculum table. These choices are independent of UCR fit.

exception.reason: PThU requires systematic theology, eight Biblical Greek and Hebrew courses and exegesis in the biblical languages. The UCR curriculum develops cultural interpretation, philosophy and ethics but lacks a progression in Christian theology or scriptural interpretation.
exception.curriculumContext: This example combines the Systematic Theology track with biblical Greek, Hebrew and exegesis. Students can also choose a route without biblical languages. The degree includes a 30 EC minor and a 15 EC final research project.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The assembled programme was reviewed against systematic theology, eight Biblical Greek and Hebrew courses and exegesis in the biblical languages. World Myth & Literature compares narratives across cultures, art and archaeology study material evidence, and Ethics examines moral arguments. These courses make substantive contributions to the study of religion in culture. They do not develop Christian doctrine or the interpretation of biblical texts as sustained subjects. Technology and health ethics likewise concern applied moral reasoning.
